timeline.body:
This removes the deprecated params `allow_no_datafeeds` and `allow_no_jobs` from v8 rest APIs.

The params still exist and are deprecated in v7 REST APIs.

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/60732

@jakelandis || @pgomulka I am not 100% sure how to handle this. I want the parameter to be deprecated in v7, but I don't want to accept `DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM` in v8. Is there a way to indicate this to the parser? Or do I need to add a new parse field for `v7` compatibility (which will have the same `allow_no_match` and `DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM`) and remove the deprecated `DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM` from this field?

reply.body:
I am pretty sure that 
```
new ParseField("allow_no_match", DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM).forRestApiVersion(RestApiVersion.equalTo(RestApiVersion.V_7)));
```
will do as you want.

you need the snippet ^^ above
note that field is declared in PARSER and when constructing a response
baller! I will try it out.

@jakelandis @pgomulka this doesn't work :(. 

```
org.elasticsearch.ElasticsearchStatusException: Elasticsearch exception [type=x_content_parse_exception, reason=[1:43] [cluster:admin/xpack/ml/datafeed/stop] unknown field [allow_no_match]]
```

We need to keep `allow_no_match` in 8 and 7 and only have the deprecated name in 7.

> We need to keep allow_no_match in 8 and 7 and only have the deprecated name in 7.

That doesn't sound like a breaking change, so wouldn't the normal deprecation (without REST API compatibility) work ?   I would assume that you would deprecate in 7.16 and leave it untouched (i.e. still deprecated) for 8.0.0 ?

or.. maybe 
in 7.16
```
new ParseField("allow_no_match", DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM)
```
in 8.0.0
```
new ParseField("allow_no_match")
new ParseField(DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM).forRestApiVersion(RestApiVersion.equalTo(RestApiVersion.V_7)));
```
(just re-read the original question and think ^^ is what you need)
_note_ - any time REST API compatibility is used a deprecation warning is logged.

@jakelandis 

If somebody calls the API with the deprecated field in v8, it should throw. 

If somebody calls the v7 version API with the deprecated field, it should log. Its been deprecated for a while now and we are removing it in 8. But rest compatibility demands we keep it.

Regular deprecation doesn't handle this as a v8 call would still allow the deprecated field.

fair point with the exception
I have double checked in our code and indeed we need to declare a field for new version as well
but I think
```
new ParseField("allow_no_match") // if you want this to be available for v7 client as well. otherwise you can narrow down to v8+ 
new ParseField("allow_no_match", DEPRECATED_ALLOW_NO_JOBS_PARAM).forRestApiVersion(RestApiVersion.equalTo(RestApiVersion.V_7)));
```
would be better, because it would emit a deprecation message indicating that a field is replaced with "allow_no_match"

take a look at this example where where a "size" was replaced with "max_docs" 
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/69037/files#diff-d1ca0854baf6d0420a6e9e8c141e9fd11ceb7a0c814a57f92bdc33bdb80cd8a6R351

awesome stuff @jakelandis && @pgomulka !

This way of handling rest versioning is fairly painless now that I grok it :)

Seems like a good opportunity for a nice refactor.
